newsitem.title: USA: Dow index drops 120 points in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Dow index drops 120 points in heavy trading.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average raced lower as investors nailed down profits Wednesday after the blue-chip market failed for the second straight day to punch through the 8,000-point mark.
The Dow ended down 119.88 points, or 1.51 percent, at 7,842.43. An early rally stalled at 7,991.26.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,710 to 1,141 on heavy volume of 589 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
While the 30-stock Dow was under the gun after its recent jump into record ground, investors were seeking opportunities beyond the blue-chip arena.
Technology stocks drew buyers, which lifted the Nasdaq Composite index 1.53 points to 1,486.63, its fifth consecutive closing record high.

With the Dow unable to rally through the magic 8,000 level, Investors began to take profits in earnest, and the afternoon was marked by a wave of sell programmes that briefly dragged the Dow below 7,800.
"It might have registered in some people's consciousness that 8,000 was pretty high," said Charles Pradilla, an analyst at Cowen & Co.
"This was just a bit of a big cap correction," he said. "We had a very, very big move, a lot of these stocks had gotten overvalued and now some money's coming out."
Analysts said the blue-chip market may pause in the near term but it appears to have enough backing to rally the Dow through the 8,000 mark.

"I expect it to hesitate a bit, see some psychological resistance at 8,000, but I think the ingredients are in place to overcome it short term," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities Inc.
Nie said his data indicated that stock valuations had not yet hit levels that would indicate a near-term pullback.

"I'm willing to speculate two to three more decent days for this phase are possible before we hit the overbought hurdle," he said. "That ought to be enough to get us comfortably above the 8,000 level."
Whatever money was being pulled from blue chips appeared to find a new home in the bond market and among tech stocks.
The 30-year Treasury rose 7/32, or $2.19 on a $1,000 bond,lowering its yield to 6.56 percent from 6.59 percent Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

The gains in technology stocks were strongest among computer network companies, with Cisco Systems Inc. up 1-5/8 to a 52-week high 76-5/16 and 3Com Corp. jumping 2-9/16 to 52-5/8 after Merrill Lynch upgraded the stocks.
"Three months ago, you couldn't give these stocks away and now you can't buy them fast enough," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capital markets at Cruttenden Roth.

Analysts doubted that the investors' rotation reflected significant fundamental problems with the blue-chip stocks, noting the Dow had risen nearly 25 percent between April 11 and its record close Tuesday of 7,962.31.
They said that at its current lofty levels, the Dow had simply run out of upside room.

"It seems like we got to what was fair value," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "According to our valuation models, 7,950 was enough and it's certainly possible there were others today reaching the same conclusion.

Among individual issues, Detroit Diesel Corp. rose 2-1/8 to 25-7/8 after reaching agreement to acquire fellow engine maker Outboard Marine Corp. for $500 million. Outboard Marine fell 3-5/8 to 15-7/8.

Wells Fargo Corp. slid 18-3/8 to 260-5/8 after warning investors its second quarter earnings would fall well short of analysts' estimates. Wells Fargo blamed high costs related to its merger with First Interstate Bancorp.
Motorola rose 3-7/16 to 85-15/16, one day after it reported stronger-than-expected earnings.
Exide Electronics Group Inc. surged 7-3/4 to 20-5/8 after Danaher Corp. offered to acquire the company for $20 per share.
Exide, a maker of power supply systems and management software, said its board would review the offer. Danaher rose 1/16 to 49-7/8.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 11.21 points to 907.54. The American Stock Exchange index lost 3.09 to 631.02.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 5.46 to 473.03. The average share was down 52 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,591.402, down 79.037, or 0.91 percent.
